validation_notes: The right side of the chart shows a decline from ~230 (early June) down to a low near 190 (late July), followed by a sharp, strong rally back to ~220-224 over the last 4-5 candles. There's no flat support line being tested multiple times, nor a series of lower highs converging toward a support — instead price made one clear low around 190 and then broke out sharply upward with large green candles and rising volume. This looks like a V-shaped reversal/breakout, not a descending triangle. A descending triangle requires at least 2-3 touches on a flat support and 2-3 lower highs compressing into an apex; here the 'support' is a single low point, not a repeated tested level, and the upper trendline (lower highs) isn't clearly present either — prices were falling in a broad channel, not compressing. I disagree with the algorithm's flag; this pattern is better described as a reversal off a low, not a triangle consolidation.
